newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels kill eight civilians - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels kill eight civilians - paper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels have killed eight family members in Algeria in the latest reported attack against civilians this week, an Algerian newspaper said on Saturday.
The rebels murdered the eight on Wednesday night in Hatatba village in Tipaza province, some 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers, El Watan newspaper said.

The newspaper gave no further details on the killing which brought the number of civilians slain by rebels to more than 300 since the country's general election last month, according to newspaper reports.
Two child shepherds have been found with their throats slit in Bougara area, south of Algiers, on Tuesday, a newspaper reported earlier this week.
On Wednesday, a bomb ripped through a cinema in the working-class district of Belcourt in Algiers wounding about 20 people, an official statement said.
Algerian newspapers said up to four people were killed and more than 30 wounded in the blast.
About 60,000 people have been killed in political violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
